newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply lower after midday dive.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply lower after midday dive.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply lower on heavy fund selling against a backdrop of LME warehouse stocks that are at nine-month highs.

The market opened lower Wednesday and absorbed the news of LME stocks rising 6,350 tones to 226,950 tonnes, the highest level since Oct. 3. Funds attacked when the active September contract broke through 108.50 cents a lb.
September at 105.80, down 4.85 from Tuesday's close, while the spot month ended at 105.85 cents a lb, down 4.80 cents.

"Most of the action was fresh fund shorts," said one broker. "I wouldn't expect prices to stay at these levels. A lot of fresh shorts came into the market today. By September's first notice day, I would expect many of these positions to cover.
"But if we cannot move up from these levels, I would say we're heading for 95 cents," he added.
Fundamentally, the market looks bearish in the near term, sources said. "It's been very quiet," said one physical broker. "We've not see much business from Europe and the Far East.
"But with prices at these levels, you have to wonder if the Chinese are going to come into the market," he added. "They are typically more active buyers in the second half of the year."
In the past six weeks, LME warehouse stocks have increased 105,400 tonnes, which many merchants claim is evidence of excess copper in the nearby market.
But another merchant predicted that stocks would begin to dwindle in September, when European consumer mills return from their August shutdowns.
"Most of the material was lended to the market during the backwardation," he said. "But come September, many of those mills will be taking that metal right back out when business picks up."
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
